answer: Bond each agent identity to a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, like an opal set once into a single ring: spawning a fake identity means buying another stake, so a sybil farm cost grows linearly with every fake. New identities start with zero history and limited permissions, and only time and good behavior extend their horizon of trust, so attackers must wait before gaining influence. Cap identities per stake and slash on abuse, and the canyon between cheap talk and costly proof becomes the defense: fakes turn expensive, slow, and unprofitable.
